ImageDescription.value: This artist’s impression shows two galaxies in the early Universe. The brilliant explosion on the left is a gamma-ray burst. As the light from the burst passes through the two galaxies on the way to Earth (outside the frame to the right) some colours are absorbed by the cool gas in the galaxies, leaving characteristic dark lines in the spectrum. Careful study of these spectra has allowed astronomers to discover that these two galaxies are remarkably rich in heavier chemical elements.

ImageDescription.value:
The building at 1921 and 1921 1/2 Avenue D was built in 1889. The two-story stuccoed brick commercial building was built by John and Ernest Wegner, who operated a groceries and liquors business in the building until 1909-1910.

By 1912, Schaefer Bros. Bakery and Confectionery was operating from the building and they made substantial improvements to the building in that year. This building served as their main store and they operated other branches in Galveston.

This Building is in the National Register of Historic Places. Coordinates N 29° 18.377 W 094° 47.398

ImageDescription.value:
Historic Route 66 near Amboy, California, USA
The historic Route 66, also known as the “Mother Road”, was officially established in 1926 as one of the first highways in the United States. It connected Chicago, Illinois, with Santa Monica, California, and stretched for approximately 3,940 kilometers.
Amboy, a small town in California, played a special role along Route 66 as a rest and supply station in the Mojave Desert. As early as the 1930s, Amboy became a popular stop for travelers and truck drivers. The famous Roy’s Motel and Café, which opened in 1938, became a landmark of the town and Route 66 as a whole.
In the 1950s and 1960s, Route 66 experienced its heyday as road traffic and tourism increased significantly. Amboy benefited from this as an important stopover, but with the construction of the Interstate Highway System, particularly Interstate 40, Route 66 was increasingly bypassed from the 1970s onwards. This led to the economic decline of many towns along the route, including Amboy.
In 1985, Route 66 was officially removed from the US highway system.

ImageDescription.value: Talk about diversity; when you go to a huge city like this, you get to see all kinds of people from all over the world. We will add more about Fresh Wednesday, Tasty Thursday, the downtown buildings, and the underground city called PATH soon, when we have more time. There is so much to see and do, and you do not have to walk that far or spend much money if you do not choose to.  2.5 million people live just in Toronto, and 5.5 million in the burbs; so it is fantastic to watch them all head for work in the morning at the same time.

ImageDescription.value: Reception lounge of the spa at Amantaka luxury resort and hotel in Luang Prabang, Laos. Amantaka is one of the 34 properties operated by Aman Resorts, hospitality company founded by Indonesian hotelier Adrian Zecha in 1988, present in more than 20 countries. The hotel, located in a French colonial building, opened in September 2009. A boutique hotel, it contains 24 lavish suites, encircling a central courtyard and is designed with a mixture of traditional Lao furnishings and modern. The suites range in size from 70 to 120 square metres and include eight suites, four pool suites, eight Khan pool suites, two Mekong pool suites and two Amantaka pool suites. All of the rooms have a king-sized bed centre of the suites beneath a traditional high ceiling. They are painted in white and have mahogany or dark wood furnishings and windows. The rooms are reported to be between 1,100 USD and 1,900 USD a night.
